args.name: Assess unfamiliar food through a controlled physical trial
args.function: Provide a reusable evidence-producing method to assess unfamiliar gathered foods, initially hazelnuts, without requiring consumption as the initial test. Measure nutrition or toxicity only if an actual supported physical test can establish them; otherwise report the limits and unresolved risks.
args.conditions: Lin has health 100 and energy 40 in mild conditions near the visible start-0-nuts plant, which has five hazelnuts. Personal knowledge does not establish hazelnut nutrition or toxicity. Appearance and growth observations do not establish edibility. Existing berry exposure trials model ordinary decay, not food safety testing.
args.inputs: A small gathered sample if needed, obtained through actual gathering. Specify any required equipment or reagents before execution; none is assumed owned or available.
args.costs: Method, time, energy and material costs are unknown. Specify them before execution, including learning requirements and any exposure risks.
args.effects: Enable supported physical testing and record measured properties, methods and limitations as personal evidence. If no non-consumptive test is supported, explicitly report that limitation rather than certifying safety. Requesting or learning alone must not create food, evidence of edibility, mastery, or wellbeing.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.

candidates.function: Place one or two whole units of an owned food on the ground as a paired exposure trial, inspect their quantity and decay, end the observation or retrieve what remains.
candidates.costs: Start: inputStackId of an owned, unspoiled, nontoxic food, quantity 1 or 2 whole units (default 2), and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: target trial in reach, one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve: operator only, one round and one energy. Cancel of an exposed trial ends observation at no cost. No supports, tools, water or fuel are used or granted.
candidates.effects: Completed setup places the samples at two ground positions 0.2 apart under the same ambient conditions; with one unit there is no matched control. No food moisture, drying or preservation model exists in this world: both samples keep the existing decay rules, so no treatment difference, preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is produced. The trial records rounds exposed and marks a 10-round observation checkpoint; ageing continues while unattended and after the checkpoint. Inspect records sample quantity and decay as a personal unverified record. Retrieve returns only the remaining material, never a replacement. Setup interruption keeps paid work; cancel releases reserved food once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for starting, inspecting or retrieving.

candidates.function: Check owned food and a stone support for air-drying and report what the world cannot yet support; no food can currently be dried.
candidates.costs: Set-up with inputStackId and supportId checks the food (owned, unspoiled, nontoxic) and the support (an owned stone piece or a stone source in reach), then fails without spending anything. Other modes fail at no cost because no batch can exist.
candidates.effects: Currently unsupported: stone records have no shape, exposed area or cleanliness, so a support cannot be validated, and this run has no food water-content or drying model. Food keeps its existing decay. No reservation, drying, preservation, safety claim or reward is produced. A working operation needs a separately decided support representation and the installation of a reviewed moisture model; none is invented here.

Remove: the arranger only, unoccupied patch, one round and one energy.
candidates.effects: A completed patch holds the reserved material in a 0.25-radius footprint used only for occupancy and drawing; no thickness, coverage, body fit, warmth, insulation or comfort is inferred. Trial-rest runs the existing rest action unchanged and records energy before and after; the patch is not a registered facility, so it adds no recovery bonus. Inspect records visible placement, remaining quantity, occupancy and tests as a personal unverified record. Remove returns the remaining material as an owned stack at the site and deletes the patch; pickup stays a separate action. Cancel releases reserved material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward, regrowth, repair or top-up.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"lin\",\"decision\":\"reuse\",\"ability\":\"probe\",\"reason\":\"The existing probe capability directly covers nearby observation and small-sample physical testing through its mode and intensity arguments. Its full contract and the related food capabilities were checked. Neither probe nor the exposure trial establishes a supported assay for nutrition or toxicity. Lin explicitly accepts reporting this limitation, so reuse probe rather than develop a duplicate assessment interface or falsely certify hazelnuts. The ground-exposure trial is not a food-safety test and additionally requires nontoxic food.\",\"specification\":\"Reuse probe, equivalence open-baseline:probe:1, handler open.probe, revision foundation-open@1; record this as code reuse. General arguments remain target, mode (observe, press, wet or heat) and intensity from 0 to 1; do not add a nutrition/toxicity readout. Target must resolve to a visible subject; physical trials additionally require a small owned sample and whatever real physical prerequisites the selected mode needs. No water, heat source, reagent, tool or assay is assumed available. Observe may target start-0-nuts within actual interaction reach and records only directly observable properties. If Lin elects a material trial, first actually gather a sample using gather (base:gather:1, forest.gather, foundation-forest@1): target start-0-nuts, quantity 1, in source interaction range, one round and 2 energy, transferring one unit from its finite stock to an actual inventory stack. The displayed stock of five is not reserved or granted by this review; execution must revalidate it. Then supply that stack's actual ID to probe; a physical trial takes one round, 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit. Observation takes one round and 0.2 energy without sample consumption. Gather plus one physical trial therefore requires two action rounds, 2.5 energy and 0.1 unit of the gathered sample, excluding travel and normal world costs. Debit material exactly once; consumed trial material cannot also remain edible inventory. Retain the surviving quantity under existing ownership and decay rules; no food, reagent or replacement stock is created. Wet and heat modes must not fabricate their missing physical inputs; use only an executable supported mode. Report only the measured response implemented by that mode, with target/sample identity, mode, intensity, time, actual inputs, outcome and limitations. A mode name, visual appearance, softening, crushing, ordinary decay or lack of visible change cannot establish nutritional value, toxicity, absence of toxins or general edibility. No supported non-consumptive nutrition/toxicity assay is demonstrated in this registry: explicitly report those properties as unresolved without reading hidden resource values. Do not use eating, tasting or exposure of another participant as an implicit test. No health or satiety improvement results from inspection or sample testing. A complete probe is one indivisible interaction; interruption cancels it, with no resumable fractional test or completed evidence. Retry is a new action with newly validated inputs and costs. Preserve any already incurred effort or material loss; cancellation or death never regenerates spent inputs. Unconsumed material remains governed by existing inventory/death rules, with no duplicate refund. Gather uses its existing interruption and surviving-escrow rules. No persistent apparatus, ongoing trial, maintenance obligation or unattended treatment is created; remaining food continues ordinary ageing. Requests, learning and development/review waiting do not execute these actions or advance the world. Enforce these restrictions through the reused execution handler rather than repeated model adjudication.\",\"learning\":0,\"experienceReview\":\"Lin uses the existing zero-duration baseline individually; this review grants neither mastery nor evidence. Reuse the visible plant or real sample appearance; do not create a laboratory, assay equipment, edible/safe marker, nutrition meter or success animation from the request. Distinguish completed observation or manipulation from a positive food-safety result: the former may succeed while nutrition and toxicity remain unresolved.
